# Go7 Workhorse

> One desk for every AI subscription you already pay for. A native desktop app for Windows and macOS that runs Grok, Claude, Codex, Cursor and your own API keys side by side, each under its own login. Pick a model per chat or let it route by task with a reserve you set. See what each vendor has left this week, before the bill. Open source under MIT. Runs on your machine; there is no hosted service and no account with us.

## Why it exists

It began at a desk paying for SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor, Claude and Codex, where one plan ran dry most days while another sat idle. The sharpest case is Grok with Cursor: a Grok plan and a Cursor plan each give you Grok 4.6, on separate meters. Workhorse treats them as one model with two pools — it shows both meters, moves a chat between them, and with auto-route on leans each task toward the pool with more left, so a plan you already pay for gets used before another is spent. The same holds for any two subscriptions that overlap. Optimising several subscriptions at once, without pooling or sharing them, is the job.

## Who it is for

- Someone who holds two or more AI subscriptions or API keys — Grok on any plan, Claude, Codex, Cursor, or an Anthropic- or OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted or local — and wants one place to choose which one does each job.
- Someone who wants that choice to stay theirs: a model per chat, or auto-routing by task (quick, balanced, deep) that can be turned off, with a weekly reserve per vendor.
- Someone who wants the work to run locally, under their own logins, with per-vendor usage visible.

## Who it is not for

- One vendor, happy in that vendor's own app.
- Anyone who wants a hosted service. This is a desktop app.
- Linux users today: installers ship for Windows and macOS.

## What it does with accounts and data

- Each vendor runs through its own CLI or API under its own login. Nothing is pooled, proxied, or shared between vendors.
- API keys are stored in the OS credential store (Keychain on macOS, DPAPI on Windows), never in plain text. If that store is unavailable, the key is not saved.
- Network: the vendors you connect (their CLIs and their usage endpoints for the meters) and GitHub, to check for a newer release. No analytics.
- Learning memory is a SQLite file on the user's disk, exportable and wipeable from Settings. Nothing is sent anywhere to hold it.
- Permission mode (ask, accept-edits, always-approve, plan) and sandbox profile (off, workspace, read-only, strict) are set per chat and shown on it. Every tool prompt from every vendor lands in one inbox.
